content: Don’t quite think “siphoned off” is the correct term. It’s capex for massive revenue increase or margin increase down the line. $AMZN is probably my favorite hyperscaler right now and example to give. Amazon’s headcount is absurd, like ~1.57M. If the capex goes into automating their workforce with LLMs. Then transitioning into physical AI: - things from self driving (deliveries) - robotics (Amazon warehouses, shipping automation). + revenue increase from building out AWS compute with Trainium and possibly selling chips too with the Neocloud strat. It’s probably the clearest path forward compared to every hyperscaler out there. $TSLA optimus use case targets is extremely broad as a pitch, but Amazon already has a specific reason to scale robotics for internal opex optimization. As for $GOOGL, probably 2nd right now, AI capex was necessary for defending its Google Search moat Gemini from ChatGPT They also have Google Cloud revenue with efficient TPUs + can sell TPUs like Nvidia GPUs. Gemini user volumes keep going up (despite the lack of contention in frontier benchmarks); and AI strategy to be working for ad optimization too. But there’s less clear paths with physical AI stuff ig? Microsoft and Meta are still trying to convince the market why capex is necessary, (we’re kinda seeing that in effect with Meta’s 30%+ Y/Y revenue growth), but doesn’t look like they’re convinced. As for market narratives, Microsoft Maia seems to be behind, their AI development was stunted from OpenAi investments, so sentiment is kinda in the ground. But think that will change down the road like the 180 with Google. I’m sure all the hyperscalers are seeing the leader effect right now: If you have the leading LLM, people will keep using it. That LLM gets smarter from all the training data; and that gap might be structural. Which is why everyone is kinda rushing the buildout right now, but for some the immediate incentives seem obvious.
translated: 不太认为“吸走”是正确的术语。这是用于大幅增加收入或提高利润率的资本支出。 $AMZN 可能是我现在最喜欢的超大规模提供商，也是我举的例子。亚马逊的员工人数很荒谬，大约有 157 万。如果资本支出用于通过法学硕士实现劳动力自动化。然后过渡到物理人工智能： - 自动驾驶（送货） - 机器人（亚马逊仓库、运输自动化）。 + 通过使用 Trainium 构建 AWS 计算以及可能通过 Neocloud strat 销售芯片来增加收入。与现有的所有超大规模提供商相比，这可能是最清晰的前进道路。 TSLA optimus 的用例目标非常广泛，但亚马逊已经有一个具体的理由来扩展机器人技术以优化内部运营支出。至于$GOOGL，现在可能排名第二，人工智能资本支出对于捍卫其谷歌搜索护城河Gemini免受ChatGPT的影响是必要的。他们还通过高效的TPU获得谷歌云收入+可以像Nvidia GPU一样销售TPU。 Gemini 用户量持续上升（尽管前沿基准测试中缺乏争议）；人工智能策略也将致力于广告优化。但是物理人工智能的路径还不太清晰吗？微软和 Meta 仍在试图说服市场为什么资本支出是必要的（我们看到 Meta 的同比收入增长超过 30%），但看起来他们并没有被说服。至于市场叙述，微软 Maia 似乎落后了，他们的人工智能发展受到 OpenAi 投资的阻碍，所以市场情绪有点根深蒂固。但我认为这会像 Google 带来的 180 度转变一样发生变化。我确信所有超大规模企业现在都看到了领导者效应：如果你拥有领先的法学硕士，人们就会继续使用它。法学硕士从所有培训数据中变得更加聪明；这种差距可能是结构性的。这就是为什么现在每个人都在急于扩建，但对于某些人来说，直接的激励似乎是显而易见的。
